high.title: Peso Sinks on Latest US-Iran Attacks
high.summary:
The Philippine Peso weakened by 15 centavos to close at P61.56 against the US dollar on Thursday, down from P61.41 the previous session, driven by a spike in global oil prices following renewed US-Iran military exchanges. The pair opened flat at P61.41, briefly touched a session high of P61.345 (intraday PHP strength), before selling pressure pushed it to a session low of P61.58.

**Why it matters:** The Philippines is a net oil importer, meaning oil price surges driven by geopolitical risk are doubly negative for the Peso — they widen the trade deficit (putting structural pressure on PHP) while simultaneously stoking imported inflation. For FX traders, the P61.58 intraday low is now a key resistance level to watch. Should US-Iran tensions escalate further, PHP could test the P62.00 level. Bond investors should monitor whether rising oil prices feed into headline inflation prints, which could complicate the BSP's rate-cutting trajectory. Risk-off positioning in EM currencies broadly may add additional headwinds to PHP in the near term.

high.title: Philippines to Revamp Bond Pricing Ahead of JPMorgan Index Inclusion
high.summary:
The Philippine government is planning a significant overhaul of its local-currency bond pricing methodology by stripping out the impact of withholding tax — a structural reform being executed in two stages, with the first phase expected before year-end. The move is directly linked to the Philippines' anticipated inclusion in JPMorgan's Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets (GBI-EM), one of the most closely tracked EM fixed income benchmarks globally.

**Why it matters:** This is a landmark development for Philippine government bond (PhilGov) markets. JPMorgan index inclusion would trigger **passive inflows** from global bond funds mandated to track the GBI-EM, potentially bringing billions of dollars into the PHP-denominated bond market — a structurally bullish catalyst for both PHP and local bond prices (i.e., lower yields). However, the pricing methodology change may **impose mark-to-market losses on existing investors** who bought bonds under the old withholding tax-inclusive pricing framework, creating near-term volatility and potential selling pressure. Bond investors should closely track the official announcement timeline for Phase 1, monitor secondary market liquidity dynamics as the reform approaches, and assess their existing portfolio exposure to potential repricing losses. This is arguably the most significant structural reform for Philippine fixed income in years.

high.title: BSP: July Inflation Likely Settled at 5.6%-6.6%
high.summary: The BSP has projected July 2026 headline inflation within a 5.6%–6.6% range, which — if confirmed — would mark a four-month low. The central bank attributes the potential moderation primarily to easing food prices, though these gains are being partially offset by higher fuel and electricity costs, as well as persistent peso weakness. Critically, even at the low end of the range, inflation remains well above the BSP's 2%–4% target midpoint of 3%, reinforcing the case for a continued hawkish or at minimum hold posture on monetary policy. For FX traders, elevated inflation constrains BSP's ability to cut rates to defend growth, keeping the PHP under a dual pressure of import-driven price increases and tight monetary conditions. Bond investors should note that above-target inflation sustains upward pressure on government bond yields, particularly at the short end of the curve. The official PSA inflation print is due in early August — the actual figure versus this BSP estimate will be a critical near-term catalyst. Watch for any BSP forward guidance accompanying the official release, as it will signal the pace of any potential easing cycle.

high.title: June Trade Gap Widens to $4.94 Billion
high.summary: The Philippines' merchandise trade deficit widened sharply to $4.94 billion in June 2026, a 12.3% deterioration from the $4.40 billion gap recorded in the prior month, according to PSA preliminary data. The expansion in the deficit was driven by AI-related technology demand, which spurred double-digit growth in both exports and imports — though import growth outpaced exports. For FX markets, a widening trade deficit is structurally negative for the PHP/USD rate, as it signals increased demand for USD to settle import bills, compounding existing peso depreciation pressures. Combined with above-target inflation (see Article 1), the current account dynamics remain a key vulnerability for the peso. Bond investors should monitor whether the wider trade gap feeds through to a deteriorating current account, which could pressure foreign reserve adequacy and affect the BSP's capacity to intervene in FX markets. This data reinforces a cautious outlook on PHP in the near term.

high.title: National Government Outstanding Debt Jumps to Record P19.07 Trillion
high.summary: The National Government's total outstanding debt surged to a record P19.07 trillion as of end-June 2026, rising 2.8% month-on-month from P18.55 trillion at end-May — an increase of P518.98 billion driven by net availment of both domestic and external borrowings. For Philippine government bond (PGB) investors, the record debt level is a critical signal on sovereign credit trajectory and supply dynamics. Elevated and rising debt stocks suggest continued heavy issuance in the domestic bond market, which may sustain or push yields higher through a supply-demand imbalance. The growing external borrowing component also introduces FX refinancing risk, particularly given peso weakness and a wide trade deficit. For PHP traders, rising sovereign debt denominated in foreign currency increases USD demand at rollover periods and can weigh on the peso. Rating agencies and foreign investors will be watching the debt-to-GDP trajectory closely. This development warrants monitoring alongside fiscal deficit data and BTr issuance calendars in the coming months.

high.title: Peso May Stay at P61:$1 Level
high.summary: The Philippine Peso closed at P61.24 per USD on Friday, strengthening 32 centavos from Thursday's P61.56 — its strongest finish in over a month since June 29's P61.17 close. Market consensus points to continued sideways trading in the P61 range this week, with direction contingent on two key drivers: global oil price movements (elevated oil imports weigh on the current account and exert PHP depreciation pressure) and the upcoming release of key domestic economic data, likely the July CPI print. For FX traders, the near-term technical floor appears well-anchored at P61, but upside USD pressure could re-emerge if oil rebounds or inflation data surprises to the upside — reinforcing BSP hawkishness and risk-off sentiment. Bond investors should monitor the CPI release closely, as a hotter-than-expected print could reprice rate-cut expectations and push yields higher across the curve. The peso's resilience despite global volatility suggests supportive FX inflows or BSP intervention in the background. Watch: July CPI release, oil price trajectory, and any BSP commentary on FX intervention.

high.title: T-Bill and Bond Rates May Be Mixed Before CPI Data
high.summary: Government securities rates are expected to trade mixed this week as market participants adopt a wait-and-see stance ahead of the release of key Philippine economic data — most critically the July CPI figures — against a backdrop of renewed inflation concerns that could reinforce central bank hawkishness globally. The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) is set to auction P50 billion in T-bills on Monday (P20 billion each in the 91- and 182-day tenors, P10 billion in 364-day papers), followed by a P30 billion reissued T-bond offer on Tuesday. For bond investors, the mixed rate outlook reflects the market's uncertainty: if CPI comes in elevated, yields could rise as rate-cut bets are pared back; a softer print could rally bonds. The BTr auction results will serve as an important sentiment barometer. Traders should monitor bid-to-cover ratios closely as a gauge of risk appetite and liquidity conditions heading into the data release.

high.title: Government Debt Yields Slip as Players Turn Defensive Amid Volatility
high.summary: Philippine government securities (GS) yields declined an average of 2.33 basis points week-on-week as of July 31, per PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service (BVAL) Reference Rates on the Philippine Dealing System. The short end of the curve led the move, with 91- and 364-day T-bill yields falling 3.63 bps, reflecting defensive positioning by market players amid volatile oil prices and a hawkish-pause stance from the US Federal Reserve. The simultaneous decline in yields (price rally) and defensive posture suggests a flight-to-safety dynamic within the domestic bond market rather than a clear directional easing bet. For bond investors, the flattening bias at the short end may offer selective opportunities, but the broader curve direction remains hostage to the upcoming CPI release and Fed communication. The Fed's hawkish pause is a critical external anchor — any shift in US rate expectations will have direct implications for Philippine bond yields and capital flow dynamics. Watch for the full curve breakdown and whether the rally holds through this week's BTr auctions.

high.title: Poll: Philippine Inflation Steady at 6.4% in July
high.summary:
Headline inflation in the Philippines is forecast to have held steady at 6.4% year-on-year in July, according to a BusinessWorld poll of 21 analysts. Lower food prices — most notably rice — offset higher fuel and electricity costs. Critically, this would mark the **fifth consecutive month** that inflation has breached the BSP's 4% upper target ceiling, and represents a dramatic surge compared to the 0.9% recorded in the same month a year prior.

**Why it matters:** Persistently elevated inflation well above the BSP's target band significantly constrains the central bank's ability to cut policy rates, even as growth momentum appears to be weakening (see GDP article below). This stagflationary dynamic is particularly negative for PHP, as it complicates the BSP's rate path and may dampen foreign appetite for Philippine assets. Bond investors should watch for upward pressure on short-to-medium tenor yields as rate cut expectations get pushed further out. The official PSA inflation print release will be the key near-term catalyst to monitor.

high.title: Q2 GDP Growth Likely Slowed to 2.8% — Poll
high.summary:
The Philippine economy is projected to have expanded by just 2.8% year-on-year in Q2 2026, based on a BusinessWorld poll of 21 economists — a notable deceleration from prior quarters. The slowdown is attributed to elevated inflation weighing on household consumption, weak business confidence, and sluggish public infrastructure disbursements.

**Why it matters:** A GDP print at or below 2.8% would represent a significant growth miss and reinforces a stagflationary narrative — slowing growth paired with stubbornly high inflation. This creates a difficult policy dilemma for the BSP: cutting rates risks stoking inflation further, while holding rates steady deepens the growth drag. For PHP traders, a weak GDP print could trigger risk-off sentiment and peso depreciation pressure. PSEi sentiment is also vulnerable, particularly for rate-sensitive and consumer-facing sectors. Watch for the official NEDA/PSA GDP release and any subsequent BSP commentary on the growth-inflation tradeoff.

high.title: Cautious Trading Likely Before Inflation and GDP Data
high.summary:
Philippine equities are expected to remain in a cautious, range-bound mode this week as markets await official July inflation and Q2 GDP data releases. The PSEi fell 1.09% (−69.31 points) to close at 6,236.44 on Friday — the benchmark's worst close in recent sessions — while the broader All Shares Index dropped 0.59% to 3,395.05. Lingering geopolitical risk from the Middle East is also cited as an additional headwind dampening investor risk appetite.

**Why it matters:** The PSEi is clearly repricing ahead of potentially negative macro data. A close at 6,236 is a technically significant level to watch for support. If inflation confirms at 6.4% and GDP underwhelms at ~2.8%, expect further downside pressure on the index and potential PHP weakness as foreign investors may reduce local equity exposure. Fund managers should watch foreign net buying/selling flows on the PSE as a leading indicator of broader capital flow direction.

medium.title: BSP Sets Three-Phased Evaluation Process for Payment System Operators' Registration
medium.summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has issued updated guidelines governing the registration of operators of payment systems (OPS), superseding rules established nearly seven years ago. Under a memorandum signed by BSP Deputy Governor Mamerto E. Tangonan, the new framework introduces a structured three-phased evaluation process: (1) verification of eligibility, (2) assessment of legal documents and business models, and (3) issuance of registration certificates. While this is primarily a regulatory and operational development rather than a direct monetary policy signal, it is relevant to fund managers tracking BSP's broader mandate over financial infrastructure, digital payments, and systemic risk oversight. A more robust and transparent OPS registration regime can enhance confidence in the Philippine financial system's regulatory architecture, which has positive longer-term implications for foreign investor perception of the banking sector and capital market integrity. No immediate impact on PHP, yields, or PSEi is expected, but this reflects the BSP's continued institutional strengthening efforts.

medium.title: Metrobank Books P12.3-Billion Net Profit in Q2
medium.summary: Metrobank, one of the Philippines' largest universal banks, reported a Q2 net profit of P12.3 billion, marginally down 2.33% year-on-year from P12.59 billion in Q2 2025, bringing first-half earnings to P24.902 billion — broadly flat versus P24.846 billion in H1 2025. The slight earnings dip was attributed to higher provisioning and lower trading gains amid market volatility, even as interest income remained resilient. As a systemically important bank, Metrobank's results are a proxy for broader sector health; sustained interest income suggests lending activity and net interest margins remain supported under the current rate environment, while elevated provisioning signals management caution over asset quality risks, potentially tied to geopolitical or domestic macro uncertainties. Investors in Philippine bank equities and bonds should note that trading income headwinds reflect the volatile fixed-income environment, consistent with bond market dynamics worth monitoring.

medium.title: Lower Costs, Spending Pickup Lift Business Confidence in June
medium.summary: The BSP's monthly Business Expectations Survey (BES) showed the confidence index (CI) recovering to 0% in June from a deeply negative -25.2% in May, ending three consecutive months of negative sentiment. The improvement was attributed to lower oil prices easing input costs and a consumer spending uptick tied to the reopening of schools. While a neutral CI is far from exuberant, the sharp reversal from May's lows suggests stabilization. For macro traders, this data point mildly reduces near-term recession risk concerns and provides tentative support for domestic demand assumptions embedded in BSP growth forecasts — a marginally supportive signal for PSEi sentiment and PHP stability.

medium.title: June Loan Growth Slows to Four-Month Low
medium.summary: BSP data showed universal and commercial bank loan growth decelerated to 9.8% year-on-year in June (to P14.882 trillion), down from 12.1% in May and the slowest pace in four months, as businesses turned cautious and consumer demand softened under challenging macroeconomic conditions. The slowdown in credit expansion signals cooling domestic economic momentum, which is relevant to the BSP's monetary policy calculus — weaker credit growth reduces inflationary pressure from the demand side and could strengthen the case for further rate cuts. For bond investors, a softer credit cycle is generally supportive of lower yields; for PHP, the growth moderation is a mild negative but may be offset if BSP cuts are already priced in.

medium.title: PSEi Falls as Market Weighs Fed and SONA Signals
medium.summary:
The PSEi declined 0.74% or 47.29 points to close at 6,305.75 on Thursday, with the all-shares index also falling 0.92% to 3,415.35, as investors remained cautious following the US Federal Reserve's latest policy communications and digested reform proposals from President Marcos' State of the Nation Address (SONA). The Fed's stance is particularly relevant as it directly influences PHP/USD dynamics and the attractiveness of Philippine assets relative to US dollar-denominated alternatives. A prolonged high-rate environment in the US limits BSP's room to cut, while SONA-related policy uncertainty adds a domestic risk premium. Equity market weakness, if sustained, could signal broader risk-off sentiment that may also weigh on PHP and trigger capital outflows from both the bond and equity markets — a key dynamic to monitor heading into the August trading sessions.

---

medium.title: BSP Bills' Rate Edges Up as Bids Drop
medium.summary: The BSP's 28-day bills saw their average yield edge slightly higher at the latest auction, even as total tenders of P43.39 billion exceeded the P40 billion offer size. However, the bid-to-cover ratio fell sharply to 1.08x from 1.55x in the prior week, signaling a notable drop in demand for BSP's short-term liquidity absorption instruments. The decline in subscription appetite could reflect shifting bank liquidity preferences or early positioning ahead of upcoming CPI and macroeconomic data. For monetary policy watchers, a reduced bid-to-cover on BSP bills alongside a marginally higher yield is a nuanced signal — it may suggest that banks are less eager to park excess funds at the BSP, potentially hinting at tighter near-term liquidity or a preference to deploy funds elsewhere. This bears watching as a leading indicator of domestic liquidity conditions and its interaction with BSP's monetary stance.

medium.title: BPI Plans to Pilot Stablecoin Remittances in Fourth Quarter
medium.summary: Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), one of the country's largest banks, plans to pilot stablecoin-based remittance rails in Q4 2026 through a partnership with digital clearing house Meridian, with fiat currency conversion retained at the point of settlement. While primarily a fintech/banking development story, this has medium-term relevance for OFW remittance flows — a critical source of FX supply for the Philippines (historically ~$3+ billion/month). If stablecoin rails accelerate remittance settlement efficiency and reduce costs, they could modestly boost net FX inflows over time. Near-term FX impact is limited given pilot-stage rollout, but the BSP's regulatory posture on stablecoin remittances will be worth monitoring as a signal for broader digital asset integration into the Philippine financial system.

medium.title: BSP to Crack Down on Online Lenders' Unfair Debt Collection Practices
medium.summary:
The BSP has signaled it will prioritize issuing regulations targeting predatory lending and abusive debt collection practices by online lending companies (OLCs) once it formally assumes full supervisory oversight of the sector. BSP General Counsel Roberto Figueroa confirmed the central bank's intent to enforce tighter conduct standards as part of the transition. While this is a regulatory/consumer protection development rather than a direct monetary policy signal, it is relevant as it reflects the BSP's expanding supervisory mandate and its focus on financial system integrity. For banking sector investors, this may affect fintech-adjacent lenders and signals a more interventionist regulatory posture from the BSP going forward.
